verdict_note: From reading only: no build, no clippy, no test run. Line anchors are at f6b041c2. The mechanism holds for every layer that has content or is a plain null: the port is lazy, typed, cancel-aware, one undo step, and the layer-alone evaluation is value-equal to the whole-composition one (see answers.layer_alone). One high defect: for a CAMERA or LIGHT layer the renderer does not use transform_parts for an absent position (it uses the composition centre), so the port keys [0,0] and the key moves the camera or light (F1). The fix is one refusal in an owned path plus one test. F2 to F6 are low or notes.

findings.what: The implied position of a camera or light is not transform_parts' value. camera_at and lights_at read l.streams.position themselves and default an absent stream to the composition centre. transform_parts gives a Content::None layer position [0,0]. The port returns ([0,0],[0,0]) for a camera or light, harness-core creates a static_implied position stream keyed [0,0], and from then on camera_at / lights_at sample [0,0] instead of the centre.
findings.scenario: Media Viewer, composition 1920x1080 with one 3D raster layer. composition.add_layer kind camera (no position stream). property.enable_animation {layer_id: camera, property: position, time: T} (or keyframe.add_at_current / toggle_at_current). Accepted; the stream holds one key [0,0]. The active camera moves from (960, 540, -zoom) to (0, 0, -zoom): every 3D layer of the composition shifts in every frame. The same for a light: its position moves from the centre to the corner and the shading changes. Undo restores it; disable restores it (static_implied), but the command itself changed the render.
findings.fix: In implied_value (owned path), before the port: refuse property_default_unknown when the layer is a camera or a light (l.camera.is_some() || l.light.is_some()) and the property is position. Simplest: refuse both anchor and position for such a layer (the anchor is not read by camera_at or lights_at). State it in the module docs and in layer_anchor_position's doc ('not for a camera or light layer'). Not recommended here: returning the composition centre, because the renderer is not consistent for a camera or light that is a PARENT (F2), so no single value is right.

answers.layer_alone: EQUAL for every layer kind except camera and light layers (F1), where the difference is not caused by the alone evaluation: the whole-composition accessor would return the same wrong [0,0]. Dependencies of transform_parts (composition.rs:1334-1364): only l.content (bounds, origin) and l.streams (anchor, position, scale, rotation), sampled at the composition tick. It does not read parent, matte, clipped, mode, timing, pin, masks, three_d, effects, collapse, motion records or any sibling; there is no auto-orient in this file. The parent chain is applied afterwards in matrix() (:1392-1416) and parent_3d (:1664), on top of the stored position, so position is in the parent's space and does not depend on the parent. l.content is built in read() (:945-1017) from: (1) raster tiles: the layer's own tile rects (bounds_of); (2) precomposition: Rect(0,0,nested.width,nested.height) from the nested composition HEADER (:951-960), never from its layers, so an empty nested copy gives the same centre; collapse_transformations changes how the nested layers are spliced, not the bounds or transform_parts; (3) static path (enabled mask, or with prepared inputs text/vector/records): static_content (:514-681) lowers and evaluates the DOCUMENT snapshot rooted at the layer's graph operation, with the same RenderInputs::default() the render queue uses (render_queue.rs:576); the composition enters only as Rect(0,0,comp.width,comp.height) for an unlinked vector mask, and the header is kept; DocumentTiles holds the layer's own tiles, which is all a subtree rooted at that layer names; (4) group, null, composition adjustment, empty raster (solid or shape host): Content::None, [0,0] and [0,0], and the solid's motion content is drawn with that same matrix. So siblings, parent, mattes, the nested layers, collapse and auto-orient do not enter the stored anchor or position. The only composition renderer in the product (render_queue.rs:565-580) uses the same inputs, so there is no second reading to disagree with. What the alone build changes is refusals only: a sibling the reading cannot build, a matte or adjustment rule (:1035-1047), or a dangling parent no longer refuses this layer's value. UNVERIFIED: a layer effect that references another composition layer could make the alone records fail validation (a refusal, never a wrong value).
